title: Demonstrators protest across France against high living costs and government policies

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, high fuel and energy prices, and government budgetary measures.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand higher wages, a 10% or 100-to-150-euro increase in the minimum wage, and the defense of public services and jobs.

summary: Thousands of people took to the streets across France, including in Paris, for a new weekend of demonstrations marking the fourth consecutive weekend of protests against the rising cost of living and government policies. The movement originated with high school and university students and has been joined by labor unions and the Yellow Vests movement. Protesters marched to demand wage increases, better purchasing power, and the defense of public services. In Paris, clashes occurred at the end of the march between security forces and individuals throwing projectiles, while a separate banned rally by the Yellow Vests near the National Assembly was blocked by police. According to the Interior Ministry, 146,000 people protested nationwide with 46,000 in Paris, whereas trade unions reported 250,000 protesters nationwide and 75,000 in the capital. Following these demonstrations, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened a social conference on November 9 to address the crisis.
demands: Protection of public services, jobs, and industry
Action against high housing, fuel, and food costs
response: Police deployed 70,000 officers nationwide, used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles in Paris, and blocked a banned rally near the National Assembly. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened a social conference on November 9, offering a minor minimum wage increase which unions dismissed as inadequate.

crowd.text: Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital.

updates.text: Thousands protested across France for a fourth weekend against living costs, with clashes reported in Paris.
French citizens maintained pressure on the fourth Saturday of mobilization, with a banned Yellow Vests rally blocked near the National Assembly.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened a social conference with unions and employers to address wage and purchasing power demands.
